projects.description:
Proximity Sensor – Countertop Kiosk Specification
1. Overview
Farmers Hub wishes to install a customer proximity sensor on a countertop promotional kiosk located on top of refrigerated display units in BP service stations.
The kiosk displays promotional messages and videos highlighting the day's fresh, direct-from-farm produce. Its purpose is to attract customers' attention while they are waiting in the queue to pay.
The proximity sensor will automatically activate the kiosk when a customer approaches, ensuring promotional content and audio are only active when customers are nearby.

2. Functional Requirements
The proximity sensor should provide the following functionality:
A. Customer Detection
• Detect customers approaching the kiosk from approximately 5 metres away.
• Detection distance should ideally be configurable to suit different store layouts.
• The sensor should reliably detect customers approaching from the front of the kiosk.
B. Automatic Activation
When a customer is detected, the sensor should:
• Wake the kiosk from hibernation or sleep mode, if applicable.
• Activate the kiosk's audio and set the volume to a predefined level.
• Start or resume promotional content playback.
C. Activation Duration
• The activation period should be configurable by Farmers Hub (e.g. 2–5 minutes).
• If no further customers are detected during this period, the kiosk should automatically return to its previous standby state.
• If another customer is detected while the kiosk is active, the activation timer should reset, keeping the kiosk active for the configured period from the latest detection.
D. Audio Control
• When no customers are detected, the kiosk volume should be set to zero or muted.
• When a customer is detected, the volume should automatically return to a predefined, configurable level.
• Volume settings should be adjustable remotely or through the kiosk configuration.

3. Customer Detection Data and Reporting
A preferred additional feature is the ability to record every new customer detection event.
This data will help Farmers Hub understand customer traffic patterns, identify peak periods and compare customer engagement with produce sales.
Each detection event should record:
• Date
• Time (24-hour format)
• Hour
• Minute
• Second
Example data record:
2026-11-15 18:45:32
The system should:
• Store each detection event with an accurate timestamp.
• Retain records locally if internet connectivity is unavailable.
• Ideally allow detection data to be downloaded or accessed remotely for analysis.
• Support exporting data in CSV or Excel-compatible format.

4. Configuration and Management
Where possible, the following settings should be configurable by Farmers Hub without requiring hardware changes:
• Detection distance (target approximately 5 metres).
• Activation duration (X minutes).
• Audio volume when activated.
• Standby volume (zero/muted).
• Data access and export.

5. Installation and Compatibility
• The sensor must be compatible with the existing countertop kiosk hardware and software.
• It should be compact and suitable for discreet installation on or within the kiosk.
• It must operate reliably in a busy service station retail environment.
• It should be suitable for continuous operation during store trading hours.
• The solution should require minimal intervention from BP store staff.

6. Preferred Outcome
A simple, reliable and cost-effective proximity sensor solution that automatically activates the Farmers Hub promotional kiosk when customers approach, controls the audio and standby behaviour, and preferably captures timestamped customer detection data for subsequent analysis. Freelancers should provide multiple sensor options with different capabilities and costs, allowing Farmers Hub to choose the most suitable solution. Freelancers should explain how their solution can be adapted for use with other kiosk models. The deliverables must include the source code, with full rights to modify and use it without incurring additional costs.

7. Repeatable process
Develop a standardised installation process that Farmers Hub can independently replicate across different kiosk models and retail locations, enabling scalable, cost-effective future deployments.
One technical consideration: I would ask suppliers to distinguish between a wake-on-detection solution and a software-controlled standby solution. Some kiosks cannot be woken from full hibernation by an external sensor without additional hardware. A USB, relay or GPIO interface may be required. This is worth identifying before selecting the sensor.

3. A brief walkthrough video or screenshots showing key user flows working end-to-end.

If you’ve built marketplace search or real-time chat features before, that’s a plus—share a link or two. Let’s craft a browsing-first freelancer platform that feels instant and effortless from the very first click.

projects.title: Customer Account Management Website
projects.description:
I need a full-featured website that lets my customers securely log in, view or update their personal details, and book, reschedule, or cancel appointments—all from a clean, mobile-responsive web interface (no separate mobile app required).

Here’s the flow I have in mind:
• New users sign up, verify their email, and create a password-protected account.  
• Once inside, they can edit profile information such as name, contact details, and preferences.  
• An integrated calendar shows available time slots so they can make a booking, move it, or cancel with instant confirmation.  
• Automatic email notifications should go out for each action.

From the back-end I’ll need an admin dashboard to:
• View and filter customer profiles and appointment logs.  
• Manually add or modify bookings when needed.  
• Export data to CSV or Excel for reporting.

Core requirements
• Modern, responsive design that works smoothly on desktop, tablet, and phone browsers.  
• Secure authentication (password hashing, session management, forgot-password flow).  
• Clearly structured database for users and appointments.  
• REST or GraphQL API endpoints so future mobile apps can be layered on later.  
• Source code, build instructions, and brief documentation delivered at hand-over.

Tech stack is flexible; suggest what you’re most comfortable shipping quickly and securely (React, Vue, or plain HTML/CSS for the front end; Node, Django, Laravel, etc. for the back end—open to discussion).

I’ll provide brand assets and copy; you handle design, development, testing, and deployment to my hosting. Let me know your proposed stack, timeline, and any similar projects you’ve completed.

projects.title: Travel Info Website with Budget Estimator
projects.description:
I want to launch an easy-to-navigate website packed with practical facts for anyone planning a trip. Each country page will show currency details, recommended hotels, signature foods, transport options, cultural insights and a concise “places to visit” section. The first batch of destinations will be Egypt, Morocco, Mauritius, Botswana, Rwanda, Namibia, Vietnam and Malaysia, with the structure kept open so I can slot in more countries later without new development.

The centrepiece is an interactive trip-cost estimator. A visitor types how many days they will stay and instantly sees a total budget in US dollars. The calculation must break the cost down into hotels, transport, food, activities and entrance fees to historical sites or museums. Costs should shift automatically when the day count changes and adapt to the price range that makes sense for the traveller; some will backpack on a shoestring, others will choose mid-range or a splash of luxury, so the logic needs to accommodate all three levels.

I need a modern, responsive design that loads fast on mobile. A lightweight CMS such as WordPress (or a headless alternative if you prefer) will let me update prices, add photos and publish new country pages myself. Clean code, basic on-page SEO, Google Maps embeds and an image gallery for each destination are highly desirable.

Deliverables  
• Fully functioning responsive website with CMS setup  
• Custom trip-cost estimator integrated and tested for the eight listed countries  
• Clear admin guide (text or short video) showing how to edit prices, add destinations and tweak the estimator formula

projects.title: AI-Powered Telegram Support Bot
projects.description:
I need a Telegram bot that can step in whenever a user asks a question and instantly craft a helpful reply through an AI assistant rather than a fixed FAQ sheet. The user’s message should pass to the AI back-end (OpenAI, Claude, or any comparable model you recommend) and the generated answer must return to Telegram in a clear, friendly tone while keeping conversation context intact.

How I picture the flow  
• User poses a question in a group, channel, or DM  
• Bot forwards it to the AI service, waits for completion  
• AI response is sent back to the user, tagged or threaded appropriately  
• Bot records basic interaction stats for me (/stats)

Core expectations  
• Clean, reliable integration with Telegram Bot API  
• Context handling so back-and-forth conversations feel natural  
• Simple admin commands (/enable, /disable, /reset, /stats)  
• Secure management of all API keys via env vars or a config file  
• Deployment instructions for a small VPS or serverless setup

I place high value on seeing your past work—especially bots or AI integrations you’ve already rolled out—so please include links or brief descriptions in your proposal. Code readability, meaningful comments, and a concise README are must-haves because I’ll want to fine-tune prompts and settings on my own later.

If you can outline how you’d stage the milestones and mention any external services or libraries you plan to rely on, that will help me lock in a decision quickly.
